title: Harper's quant & eval day brief
content:
Morning snapshot (short):
- goal: quick sanity sweep of 4-bit quantized 7B variant on dedicated nodes; collect per-token latency and answer-quality delta vs float16 baseline.
- context: yesterday's run showed a weird 6% BLEU drop on few-shot summarization prompts when using qat-like weight folding. Need to repro with deterministic seeds.

Run log (ad-hoc, copy pasta):
- run id: harper-q-20260314-1
- model: redwood-open-7b-v1 (float16 baseline)
- variant A: redwood-open-7b-v1-q4 (GPTQ fast path)
- infra: ded-pool-2 (A100s), batch size 1, max_len 512, kv_cache enabled, prefix caching off
- prompt set: rapid-sum-20 (20 examples, mixed domains; see listing below)

Quick numeric notes: (median over 20 samples)
- baseline float16: latency(token start->first_token): 38ms; avg per-token after warmup: 9.8ms; memory p95: 12.8GB
- q4 variant: latency first_token: 54ms; avg per-token: 11.7ms; memory p95: 7.2GB
- quality: ROUGE-L drop ~0.045 (absolute), human-glance shows more terse completions, occasional dropped punctuation.
- token throughput observed: baseline 102 tok/s, q4 86 tok/s (single stream)

Immediate hypotheses:
- kernel selection for q4 path picks lower-precision matmul that increases setup overhead (explains first-token bump). Need tracing to confirm where extra time spent (weight unpack? reorder?).
- quantization scale/clipping may be affecting low-magnitude weights used for punctuation/stop tokens -> visible punctuation loss.
- caching interplay: KV cache seems fine, but when prefix cache disabled some outputs become shorter. Might be prompt-token alignment issue.

Prompt set (rapid-sum-20) -- examples (abbrev):
1) "Summarize news article: <article>" (news, long)
2) "TL;DR: <research abstract>" (scientific)
3) "Explain in 2 sentences: <policy brief>" (policy)
... (mix of imperative instruct style + few-shot examples included for half of items)

Small experiments to run (ordered):
- reproduce the drop with deterministic seed & log RNG seeds (priority 1).
- enable tracing on first-token codepath (measure time in weight read/unpack, kernel launch, postproc).
- run q4 with kernel hint: use alt-mm (if available) to see if startup latency changes.
- run a 8-bit (q8) quick run to check quality/latency tradeoff (expect memory ~10GB, latency ~10.5ms).
- test with prefix caching ON for full set to compare output lengths and punctuation.

Ad-hoc CLI snippets I've used (notes to self):
- ./serve-cli --model redwood-open-7b-v1-q4 --batch=1 --max-len=512 --kv-cache=1 --trace=kernel > ~/tmp/q4-trace.log
- python bench_tokens.py --endpoint http://ded-pool-2:8080 --promptset rapid-sum-20 --runs=3 --save=harper-q4.json

Qualitative notes (human review):
- q4 outputs are slightly more "abbreviated" on the scientific abstracts (loses clause connectors).
- on conversational style tasks, coherency still OK for 3-4 turns but sometimes drops a follow-on example in few-shot prompts.

Open questions / TODOs: (short list)
- [ ] What changed between qat-augmented quant runs from yesterday and today's bin? (compare git hashes)
- [ ] Is there a particular token class (punctuation, quotes) that gets mispredicted more often under q4? (run confusion table)
- [ ] If we accept 8-bit as sweet spot, what is cost delta per 1M tokens vs q4 and float16? (back-of-envelope)
- [ ] Add automated unit to failing eval and gate in nightly if drop > 2% ROUGE-L

Notes to self about eval hygiene: 
- keep sample-level artifacts (input, reference, model output, logits snapshot for first 32 tokens) for 5 failing cases.
- pin CUDA/cuDNN versions in run metadata (avoid silent perf diff).

Evening micro-checklist (for tomorrow):
- repro deterministic run and attach trace (morning)
- ping Sasha for kernel-hint experiment (she owns patch integrated last week)
- draft mini-PR to add punctuation confusion table to eval harness

Random scrap ideas (brain dump):
- try small targeted LUT for punctuation weights (ad-hoc bias correction) and see if it reduces punctuation drop without retraining.
- test weight-per-channel clipping thresholds with 0.5x/1x/2x to see sensitivity.

End of brief.

-- Harper
(maybe branch: harper/q4-debug-2026-03-16)
